attachments.origin_landmark: oblique line of the thyroid cartilage (the laryngeal cartilages are not modeled as skeletal elements in this pass -- approximated via the adjacent hyoid attachment region)
attachments.insertion_landmark: lower border of the body and greater horn of the hyoid

innervation.root_levels: C1 fibres travelling with CN XII

actions: raises the larynx when the hyoid is fixed

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: The one infrahyoid muscle NOT supplied by the ansa cervicalis: it takes C1 fibres that hitch a ride on the hypoglossal nerve and leave it separately. Raising the larynx towards the hyoid is what tucks it under the tongue base during swallowing.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

trigger_points.location_description: Described with the infrahyoid group, between the hyoid and the thyroid cartilage.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Thyroid/hyoid region and throat; a globus sensation.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded head and neck muscle reference document (Simons DG, Travell JG, Simons LS, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, Vol 1, 2nd ed., Williams & Wilkins, 1999)
